name: Loudness
question: Sound pressure level in decibels. Every +10 dB sounds roughly twice as loud.

items.name: Quietest room on Earth (Microsoft's anechoic chamber)
items.fact: Decibels can go below zero: zero is only the faintest sound a typical ear can hear.

items.name: Threshold of hearing
items.fact: 0 dB is roughly a mosquito flying 3 m away.

items.name: Rustling leaves
items.fact: Rustling leaves are ten times the sound energy of the threshold of hearing.

items.name: A very calm room
items.fact: A quiet bedroom at night is around 25 dB.

items.name: Normal conversation (1 m)
items.fact: Normal conversation ranges from about 40 to 60 dB.

items.name: Car passing at 30 km/h (10 m)
items.fact: At low speeds electric and petrol cars sound similar: tire noise dominates.

items.name: Television
items.fact: The US EPA names 75 dB as the level to stay under to protect your hearing.

items.name: Vacuum cleaner
items.fact: 85 dB over long periods can damage hearing.

items.name: Jackhammer (1 m)
items.fact: Jackhammers are about ten times louder than a vacuum cleaner in sound energy terms.

items.name: Chainsaw (1 m)
items.fact: Chainsaw operators are required to wear ear protection.

items.name: Vuvuzela (1 m)
items.fact: Vuvuzelas became famous at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa.

items.name: Threshold of pain
items.fact: Around 120–134 dB sound starts to physically hurt.

items.name: Trumpet (0.5 m)
items.fact: A trumpet up close is as loud as the threshold of pain.

items.name: Jet engine (1 m)
items.fact: Airport ground crew wear heavy ear defenders for good reason.

items.name: Firecracker (0.5 m)
items.fact: A firecracker at arm's length can cause instant hearing damage.

items.name: Krakatoa eruption, 165 km away
items.fact: The 1883 Krakatoa eruption was heard nearly 5,000 km away.
